clusters.state_of_play: Stephen Miller took over as White House chief of staff on Monday, replacing Susie Wiles, after Republicans lost the House and Senate in the midterms. Trump, after initially signaling acceptance, has questioned the early vote numbers and ballot machines, and admitted deportation policy was 'too tough'. Jeffries, poised to be Speaker, says Democrats will focus on affordability and corruption, and a closed-door briefing on the Huang affair is scheduled. Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO after 33 years amid allegations of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Trump has arrived in China for the APEC summit in Shenzhen, with a historic first trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin plus a Thursday one-on-one with Putin on Ukraine and security guarantees. The agenda reportedly includes nuclear arms limits, with New START expired and China's arsenal above 600 warheads. Putin's nuclear briefcase was seen carried by a Russian naval officer. A US-North Korea meeting with Kim Jong Un is uncertain, and Kim's presence is up to Xi. On Monday the administration said it is moving forward with an interim rule, fiercely debated internally, requiring licenses to export AI chips if they may provide compute to China or other restricted countries, closing a remote-access loophole and curbing a data center business serving Chinese companies. Trump also says he would not mind reinstating Huang, sees no national security risk and doubts she was a spy. A 'Bring Jensen Back' petition has thousands of signatures and tech figures are lobbying for his return, but a CNBC source says Nvidia's board is not considering it and is focused on a national security investigation; the NYT reports some in the administration oppose his return, and officials are reportedly trading blame. A Friday FAA nationwide ground stop of over four hours disrupted over a million passengers; Trump blames old equipment, denies responsibility, praised Duffy and lashed out at NBC's Yamiche Alcindor; Mullin says no one will be fired. Michigan Democrats remain split over Haley Stevens endorsing Mike Rogers.
